NOVEMBER 2026
THREE THINGS TO KNOW
01
Keep the day flexible.
Show a useful plan without
turning every hour into a
commitment.
02
Let the group decide.
Make each preference visible,
with enough context for a
clear shared decision.
03
Keep the details close.
Reservations, saved places
and travel time should feel
like one calm workspace.
FIELDWORK / TRAVEL PLANNER
NOVEMBER 2026
THREE THINGS
TO KNOW
FLEXIBLE
Leave room for a detour, a late lunch, or a slower
morning without losing the shape of the day.
SHARED
Put each person’s priorities into one visible plan,
so nobody has to keep translating the group chat.
DETAILS
Keep bookings, locations and timings together,
so the next step is always easy to understand.

PROJECT GOALS
GOAL 1
Create a useful plan
with less effort.
Plan in under 10 minutes
GOAL 2
Help every traveller
feel heard by
the group.
Invite the whole group
GOAL 3
Make the next step
clear at every point
in the journey.
Find a detail in two taps

USER INSIGHTS
“I want a plan, but I don’t
want the whole weekend
to feel like a schedule.”
Mae · weekend traveller
“The hard part is knowing
what everybody really
wants to do.”
Noah · group organiser
“A booking in one app and
a place in another makes
the day feel fragmented.”
Rin · frequent city visitor
FIELDWORK / TRAVEL PLANNER
NOVEMBER 2026
“Give us a starting point, then
let the weekend stay open.
The best part is still finding
something we didn’t expect.”

USER PERSONAS
THE EXPLORER
Wants a little structure and plenty of space
for a slower morning, a new street or a
recommendation from someone nearby.
A useful plan should feel easy to change.
THE ORGANISER
Brings friends together, balances different
priorities and keeps track of bookings.
Needs one shared picture of the trip,
with clear decisions and fewer messages.

USER PERSONAS
THE EXPLORER
Wants a little structure and plenty of space
for a slower morning, a new street or a
recommendation from someone nearby.
A useful plan should feel easy to change.
THE ORGANISER
Brings friends together, balances different
priorities and keeps track of bookings.
Needs one shared picture of the trip,
with clear decisions and fewer messages.
THE LOCAL CURATOR
Knows a city through favourite places and
small discoveries. Wants to share a point
of view, not another list of landmarks.
Trust and context matter more than volume.
FIELDWORK / TRAVEL PLANNER
NOVEMBER 2026
DESIGN PROCESS
PROBLEM ALIGNMENT
Mapped the planning journey
and compared the moments
that create the most friction.
Last week
EXPLORATION
Sketched three ways to make
a shared plan easier to start,
change and understand.
This week
SOLUTION ALIGNMENT
Review the flow as one system:
from the first saved place to
the day-of-travel details.
Week 3
HANDOFF
Confirm the core interactions,
record the remaining questions
and prepare a focused pilot.
Week 4

DIRECTION 1
Start with a simple shared plan.
Make the next decision obvious, then
let the group add detail at its own pace.
Each change stays visible to everyone.

The screen shows one useful day, with
room for the unexpected along the way.
Keywords: Shared, flexible, easy to change

Source & licenses

Original design: Design Review — Figma Community, published on Figma Community. Licensed as a Community slide-deck template under CC BY 4.0.

Changes by Cogine AI: native HTML/SVG reconstruction of the complete public preview sequence; fictional Fieldwork example copy and original product-screen illustrations; portable local navigation. Source screenshots are not embedded as slides.

Implemented typography: Inter / Tinos; Inter. Implemented fonts selected by preview matching; source font not verified.

Product screens and participant icons are original demonstration artwork. Source-derived inspiration photographs, font decisions and implementation boundaries are documented in the accompanying SOURCE-NOTICES.md. Local alignment input is single-user and is not connected to Figma or a shared voting service.
